A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ACTG-ARL work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting and some reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-generation experiments on bioRxiv and PMC-patients, including baseline comparisons, downstream utility measurements, and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds schema, model-scale, oracle-choice, Aug-PE, and repeated-run evaluations.

M1.justification: The main ACTG-ARL procedure and hybrid PPO/SFT objective remain unchanged. Appendix D.3 adds an alternative instantiation using title, category, and token_count instead of eight oracle-extracted attributes, with DP-FT replacing AIM for feature generation because titles are free text.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate biomedical text synthesis using bioRxiv and PMC-patients, with the same downstream classification and next-token-prediction tasks. The added experiments vary schemas and models within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 15 adds end-to-end comparisons with the simple three-field schema and the rich eight-field schema using DP-FT for both generators. The original external baselines remain. The single-stage baseline and ACTG-SFT comparisons already appeared in v1.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation settings: a controlled schema comparison, Gemma-3-4B evaluation at epsilon=1, Qwen2.5-32B feature extraction with annotation-agreement measurement, and Gemini-based Aug-PE trajectories at epsilon=1 and 4. These are added protocols; the original dataset splits, training settings, privacy budgets, and principal metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices D.3–D.5 and D.9 add substantive tests of schema richness, model-scale robustness, dependence on the proprietary oracle, and Aug-PE sensitivity to its generating model. They investigate previously untested design dependencies. The single-stage, instruction-tuned-model, reward-hacking, and anchor/RL ablations are retained analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix D.6 and Figure 18 first report three independent random-seed runs and mean plus standard deviation for bioRxiv classification F1. This adds limited downstream uncertainty reporting, without establishing an increase from a previously documented run count. No formal significance test or full-pipeline uncertainty analysis is reported.

E6.justification: The original plots and table values are retained, while v2 adds substantial results for the new settings. These include gains from richer schemas, ACTG's advantage with the 4B model, Qwen–Gemini annotation agreement of 0.69 versus 0.84 between Gemini runs, nearly unchanged MAUVE with the alternative oracle, and Qwen-based Aug-PE outperforming Gemini-based Aug-PE. These are additional findings, not improved scores for unchanged experiments.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.3 explicitly defines PPO's policy-probability ratio and clipped surrogate objective, where v1 only identified the algorithm. This is a limited addition of formal background; the privacy accounting, existing mathematical definitions, and error-bound reasoning remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and concluding contribution claims retain the hierarchical ACTG framework, Anchored RL, improved controllability, and the same headline gains of 20% MAUVE and 50% attribute matching. Additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 replaces the single-model-size limitation with limitations concerning one model family, two sizes, and biomedical-only coverage, and introduces a discrete latent-variable interpretation. Appendix D.9 adds an explanation emphasizing initial domain alignment in Aug-PE, while Section 4.3 discusses ARL's optional computational cost for improved control.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly specifies 50,000 anchor examples, N=9, sampling and scoring runtimes, and an H100 timing for ARL. These are additional disclosures, not demonstrated changes to the existing training procedure. The code URL is retained in the abstract, although v1's explicit statement that both code and datasets are public is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to MAPLE, federated learning, and trusted execution environments when discussing future extensions. It removes the rubric-reward footnote and its Gunjal, Viswanathan, and Huang references. The main positioning relative to DP-FT, Private Evolution, and CTCL remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section ordering are retained with localized condensation and clarification. Algorithm 1 moves from the appendix into the main text, the single-stage comparison moves earlier within the experimental appendix, and the conclusion is reorganized into conclusions, limitations, and future work.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main text and bibliography, substantially reflows existing figures, and relocates Algorithm 1 into the main paper. Figures 14–18 and 21 add a schema display and five experimental plots, including error bars and iteration trajectories. Existing graphical results are preserved despite resizing and relocation.

improvement.justification: The added schema, model-scale, and oracle checks strengthen support for the original findings, while explicit anchor-data settings and costs improve reproducibility. These benefits are bounded: the added checks remain within the existing biomedical setting, uncertainty reporting covers only downstream F1, and the new statistical-significance language exceeds what the reported mean and standard deviation alone establish.
